newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares put on a late sprint on Thursday, cheered by a firm start to Wall Street trade and were then chased higher by buying related to Friday's December options expiration.
The AEX index of blue-chip stocks reversed early losses to end up 7.13 points at 625.56, well above the low at 616.51.
Dealers said volume remained at a fairly low ebb throughout the day as investors concentrated on squaring up positions ahead of Christmas but the expiry produced a late flurry of activity.
The index was bolstered by widespread gains at most of the major stocks -- Elsevier, ING, Philips, KPN and ABN AMRO.
Flag carrier KLM was active early on as the market digested comments from American Airline chairman Bob Crandall, carried in a Dutch newspaper, that it would welcome an alliance in KLM.
"We - American Airlines and also British Ariways - would welcome an alliance with KLM. We have made that quite clear to KLM chairman (Pieter) Bouw," De Telegraaf quoted him as saying.
The shares rose quickly to 49.10 guilders but after KLM denied it was in any talks with American, interest subsided and the shares slipped back to close unchanged at 47.60 guilders.
Dealers said KLM's Northwest alliance would make such a deal difficult but the speculation was enough to spark some interest.
Drinks and food concern Nutricia rose strongly after the company said it was investigating the possibility of combining some of its activites with Friesland Dairy Foods.

Nutricia said the cooperation would include all forms of cooperation between the firms in the area of consumer products in the Netherlands and Belgium and would also explore transferring dairy products production and marketing in Germany and eastern Europe.
Dealers reacted positively to the news, pushing the shares 10.30 guilders higher to 263.50, although they also noted that turnover was not heavy at 213,558.

Music and film group PolyGram had another good day, building on Wednesday's gains but dealers said there was no particular news behind the move. The shares closed up 5.70 guilders at 85.70, recouping more of their recent losses but are still lying well below the year's peak at 106.20, reached in April.
Elsevier topped the volume list and ended up 0.60 at 28.10 guilders, followed by bank ING, which rose 0.90 to 59.80.
Dealers said the options expiry tomorrow would continue to affect the market, with some predicting further gains in store for the AEX. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
